Match report as John McGinn scores twice in Scotland's win over North Macedonia at Hampden; Aston Villa midfielder gives hosts lead after McTominay and Gilmour go close; Rastoder's header levels scoring; McGinn penalty seals win after Gannon-Doak fouled; Scotland face Switzerland next
John McGinn's double rescued Scotland as they toiled to a 2-1 win over North Macedonia to keep their Nations League promotion hopes alive.
The hosts were booed off at half-time with the game goalless but there was a sense of relief - rather than joy - at the final whistle after McGinn's penalty secured the three points after Elmin Rastoder's header cancelled out the Aston Villa midfielder's opener.
The win means Scotland can still finish second in Group B1 after Slovenia were held by Switzerland, but will have to win in St Gallen on Monday and hope North Macedonia do them a favour in their final game.
Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first win at Hampden on a night when skipper Andy Robertson earned his 102nd cap to equal the appearance record held by Sir Kenny Dalglish.
The returning Scott McTominay nearly grabbed an opener after 16 minutes but he was denied by Stole Dimitrievski in the North Macedonia goal after turning and shooting sharply. The keeper then denied Che Adams and McTominay again before the Napoli midfielder attempted to recreate his famous Denmark overhead kick to no avail.
Boos rang around Hampden as the players trudged off at the interval and Billy Gilmour did little to lift the collective mood straight after the break when he fired over with the goal gaping following good work by Adams.
Scotland did take the lead soon after, however, Adams outmuscling his North Macedonian counterpart to set the onrushing McGinn away into the box before he curled his effort into the net.
Rastoder stunned Hampden less than three minutes later, leaping highest to glance his header past Angus Gunn from a corner, but Dimitrievski went from hero to villain with a little over 15 minutes remaining, bringing down Ben Gannon-Doak when the winger seemed to be running the ball out of play.
A VAR review followed, allowing McGinn to step up and deliver a first win in Glasgow for Pocognoli, but it is a performance that will raise more questions than answers.
16: BIG SAVE! Scott McTominay controls the ball with his back to the goal, then turns sharply and shoots but Stole Dimitrievski gets down well to his left and keeps it out.
22: OVER! Andy Robertson delivers a free-kick into the box but Kieran Tierney's header loops over the bar.
27: SAVE! John McGinn's corner is met by Che Adams at the front post before his header takes a big deflection. It looks like it's heading in but Dimitrievski is equal to it again.
35: OVER! McTominay tries an acrobatic effort with an overhead kick but it sails over the bar and out of play.
39: MCTOMINAY DENIED! The ball is threaded into the feet of McTominay and he shoots from a tight angle but the goalkeeper makes another save to keep it level!
46: HOW HAS HE MISSED?! Adams capitalises on a loose back pass and squares the ball to Billy Gilmour. All he has to do is guide it on target and it is a goal but he skies it over the bar!
54: GOAL! Adams outmuscles the defender before poking the ball forward allowing McGinn to race onto it before curling the opener into the back of the net.
57: GOAL! North Macedonia shock Scotland with a quickfire equaliser. The corner is whipped into the box and Rastoder is there to glance it into the bottom corner.
75: GOAL! McGinn scores from the spot to restore Scotland's lead

"I'm happy to get the first win at home. It's important and we knew before the game that it will help to build a winning culture.
"In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I'm quite satisfied about what I saw in some moments of the game, the work on the ball and off the ball.
"It was not always perfect, but I know that what we worked on in the last two days happened many times on the pitch. And for me that's very important. On top of that, we created a lot of chances that we should score.
"Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recovered a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition. We created a big chance for Billy (Gilmour) from this also. So that's a new approach of the game. Not everything was perfect, but there was a lot to take to move forward.
"After the first goal, I think we need to learn to not drop the intensity. Because after the first goal, for five minutes, I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. And we conceded a goal from a set-piece. And I had the same feeling after the second goal. So, it's something that we need to fix."
"I thought we showed glimpses of good stuff. We tried to be patient on the ball, tried to keep the ball, I think we did that well at times, but also at times it broke down because the quality wasn't there at times so we're still trying to piece it all together.
"It's a different way of playing and that's what we are working on in the training ground. It wasn't always perfect, but no international game is easy and we're all delighted in the changing room to get that win and hopefully other people have a smile on their face too.
"Every formation can be played differently, there are so many different variations of this formation. We're trying to implement what the manager and coaches want us to do on the training ground and we're working really hard.
"Yes, it's not going to be perfect right away but everything is working towards us going into the qualifiers for the Euros. We're still trying to learn it and we believe in what the manager is trying to teach us to do and we have to be patient with that.
"I know people don't see us train and see the work we're doing in the background, so I can get why people are frustrated but there is an idea behind what we are doing and like you say at times we lacked that quality.
"Obviously the Slovenia at home game made it unrealistic, or tougher [to qualify]. We'll go over to Monday and we'll give everything we can to win that game. We're in a position where we have to rely on other results."
On equaling Dalglish's appearance record: "It feels amazing for me and my family, it's an amazing achievement. I've been around here for a long time. I've had highs, I've had lows, I've sometimes had praise and had criticism."
John McGinn to Sky Sports on Andy Robertson's record-equalling night:
"Amazing - he deserves everything that is coming his way. The biggest credit I can give him is that he is always available, always willing to help his country. Whether he is at 60, 70, 80 per cent, or 100.
"I'm sure Monday will be a special occasion for him but he'll give the boring answer that it will only be special if we get three points."
It will be a night that Andy Robertson never forgets but a game most Scotland fans will blank from their collective memories fairly quickly.
The skipper equalled Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps but it was fellow Scotland stalwart John McGinn who spared the home side's blushes on a drab evening in Glasgow.
Scotland looked slow in their build-up, even if there were first-half chances, but when the goal finally did come the floodgates did not open. Instead, North Macedonia, who hadn't scored since November 18, 2025, equalised and could have gone in front.
The natives were understandably restless but were ultimately relieved when Stole Dimitrievski clumsily brought down Gannon-Doak, allowing McGinn to be the hero again.
The Aston Villa captain was quick to remind everyone that a new style takes time to bed in and that is true. Scotland are moving away from the comforts and success of the Steve Clarke era, but questions will be asked of Pocognoli's insistence on using wing-backs and one upfront at home with a comfortable win expected.

A freighter collided with a cruise ship carrying around 130 people in New Orleans, causing the paddlewheel vessel to capsize. More than 30 people were hospitalized, but all passengers survived and were accounted for.
More than 30 people were hospitalized but no deaths were reported after a freighter collided with a cruise ship on the Mississippi River in the US on Friday.
Authorities said at least 180 passengers and crew were rescued. New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno described it as "a miracle on the Mississippi," adding that none of those hospitalized had critical injuries.
Footage showed the paddlewheel cruise boat, called The American Heritage, capsizing after the impact with the much larger cargo vessel and rescue teams rushing to get people in life jackets out of the water.
The accident happened near the port of New Orleans when the freighter Atlantic Asphalt hit the cruise ship while it was docked.
"It was just chaos," local witness Devon Flanagan was quoted by news agency AP.
"You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water," he described the scene.
The company operating The American Heritage , American Cruise Lines, said in a statement that "guests and crew were evacuated, and we are deeply concerned for everyone involved."
According to AP, the cruise ship was built in 2015, is five stories tall and can hold up to 150 passengers. It was finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.
When news of the collision broke, it was initially unclear whether there were any fatalities and how many people were injured or missing.
Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry said he was on his way to New Orleans.
"We are aware of the incident on the Mississippi and we are in close contact with local officials and law enforcement," he wrote on X.
US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin wrote on social media that "we are throwing every asset we have to helping rescue missing passengers" and that his department was coordinating closely with state officials.

President Zelensky said the US had proposed ceding Ukraine's eastern city of Donbas to Russia, in exchange for Ukrainian membership of NATO, following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi this week. He reiterated that Kyiv was not willing to retreat from its territory and warned that the Kremlin's bid to change the continent's security architecture could lead to more wars.
Ukraine 's President Volodymyr Zelensky said that the United States proposed Ukraine cede land to Russia in exchange for joining NATO and that his government was in talks on "specific" security guarantees from the West.
He said that US negotiators had floated a question about Ukraine's potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for ‌joining the alliance, following the ⁠latest round of peace talks with Russia in ‌Abu Dhabi .
Zelensky reiterated his position that ⁠Kyiv was not willing to retreat from its territory. He said that if Ukraine received a ‌comprehensive security package, that includes security guarantees, a strong and well-funded Ukrainian ‌army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a referendum.
"The Americans raised a question: "What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?" This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky told reporters in remarks released by his office on Saturday.
He said the EU and NATO are Europe's only "real security", warning the Kremlin's bid to change the continent's security architecture could lead to more wars.
"This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations," Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments under embargo until Saturday. "Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That's it. There is no other security in Europe."

Acı haberi de oyuncunun kardeşi sosyal medya hesabından duyurdu. 43 YAŞINDA HAYATA VEDA ETTİ 2026 yılında hayata veda eden ünlülere eklenen bu halka Christian Cousins.
Arnold Schwarzernegger ile birlikte kamera karşısına geçtiği Kindergarten Cop (Anaokulu Polisi) ve Knots Landing gibi yapımlarla tanınan Cousins 43 yaşındaydı.
Talihsiz oyuncunun aynı babadan dünyaya geldiği üvey kardeşi Jonas Roeser, acı haberi sosyal medya sayfasından paylaştı.
Christian Cousins'ın bir dizi fotoğrafını paylaşan Roeser "Kardeşimin hayata veda ettiğini duyurmak çok zor" diye başladı satırlarına.
Cousins'in hayata veda etmeden önce karaciğer sorunlarıyla mücadele ettiğini de satırlarına ekledi. 'BÜYÜK HAYALLERİ VARDI' Roeser, Joseph adında bir ikizi de olan Christian ile ancak üniversite yıllarında tanıştığını da belirtti. Tanışmadan önce de onları TV ekranında Knots Landing dizisinde izlediğini yazdı.
Acılı kardeş "Ancak bu roller, Christian'a ait hatıralarımın sadece küçük bir parçası. O, tutku ve enerji dolu, kendine has bir karakterdi. Anlatacak büyük hikayeleri, onlardan da büyük hayalleri vardı" diye devam etti.
Roeser, Christian'ın hayata veda etmeden önce çok hasta olduğunu belirtti. Sonra da "Artık annesiyle birlikte cennette olduğuna ve çektiği acılardan kurtulduğuna inanmak bana teselli veriyor" diye yazdı. 'SENİ ÖZLEYECEĞİM' Kardeşine son veda sözlerini "Huzur içinde uyu Christian. Umarım ruhun dinleniyordur ve aradığın huzuru bulmuşsundur. Sen benim kardeşimsin ve seni özleyeceğim" diye tamamladı.
Christian ve ikizi Joey, 1983 yılında California'da dünyaya geldi. İkizler , beş yaşındayken Highway to Heaven dizisinin bir bölümünde kamera karşısına geçti. Sonra da 1987 ile 1992 arasında Knots Landirg dizisinin 60 bölümünde kamera karşısına geçti.
Christian Cousins , 1990'da Kindergarten Cop filminde Arnold Schwarzenegger ile birlikte oynadı. İkizler son olarak 1995 yılında kamera karşısına geçmişti.

Hona’da yemeğimi bitirdiğimde aklımda yalnızca beğendiğim tabaklar değil, onları hazırlayan genç şefin kurduğu düzen de vardı. Ansar Kemaloğlu ailesinin sürgünle (1944, Kırım Tatar Sürgünü) şekillenen geçmişini, çocukluğunu ve İstanbul’da öğrendiği teknikleri aynı mutfakta buluşturuyor. Bu yaşta hikâyesini anlatacak bir dil bulması kadar daha öğrenecek çok şey olduğunun bilincinde olması da etkileyici.
Taşkent’te doğup büyüyen Ansar, Alman okulunda okumuş; evlerinin yanındaki Kore pazarı, Rus arkadaşları ve farklı mutfaklarla iç içe bir çocukluk yaşamış. 18’inde İstanbul’a gelmiş, üniversitede inşaat mühendisliğiyle başladığı eğitimini gastronomiyle sürdürmüş. Doğu Asya pişirme tekniklerini Uygur restoranında çalışarak öğrenmiş, Türk mutfağına ilgisi de çalıştığı restoranlarda gelişmiş. Mısır Çarşısı’ndaki Kasım Usta’nın Taze Balıkçı’sında balık işleyerek sashimi kesimleri, lakerda ve kürleme üzerine çalışmış.
Hona’nın adı, dedesi Mustafa’nın doğduğu köyden geliyor. Menünün ön yüzündeki ıssız köy fotoğrafı ve 14 Kasım 1944 tarihi ailenin sürgün hafızasına açılan bir kapı. Ansar abisiyle Aralık 2024’te Hona Snackery’yi açmış. Abisi tekstil ürünleri satarken o da tezgâhta balık ağırlıklı atıştırmalıklar sunuyormuş. Bir yıl sonra Hona’yı restorana dönüştürmüş. Kendi elleriyle ahşap kapladığı mekânda yalın, sıcak, zanaatkârlığı hissettiren bir atmosfer var.
Asıl dikkatimi çekense bu küçük restoranın çalışma disiplini oldu. Hazırlıklar önceden tamamlanıyor, anlık pişen yemekler mutfaktan geliyor; Ansar misafirlerin önünde son dokunuşları ve tabaklamayı yapıyor.
Hona’nın menüsünde Ahıska, Uygur ve eski Türk mutfaklarının izleri Doğu ve Orta Asya teknikleriyle buluşuyor. Tutmaç bunun güzel bir örneği. Ansar’ın anlattığına göre sürgünden sonra ekonomik güçlük yaşayan Ahıska Türkleri, geleneksel yemeğin etini küçük doğrayıp kızarttıkları erişteyle ikame etmiş. O da bugün patates çorbası ve elde açılmış Uygur lagman hamurunun üzerine beluga havyarı koyarak hikâyeyi tersine çeviriyor. Tabak, Antakya tuzlu yoğurdu, tarhun ve yanık yoğurt köpüğüyle tamamlanıyor.
Mantarların öne çıktığı dil tabağını da çok beğendim. Sığır dili mantarı ve Kanlıca kültür mantarından amazake (Japon içeceği), chicken of the woods mantarından garum ve karamelize soğanla tatlandırılmış süt reçeliyle buluşuyor. Kişnişli Borodinski ekmeği ve trüf de eşlik ediyor. Hınkalsa Ahıska geleneğinden yola çıkıyor. Eskiden düğünün ertesi günü gelin evinde servis edilen, geleneksel olarak kazla yapılan yemeği Ansar levrekle yorumlamış.
Balıkçı helvası da akılda kalıcıydı. Helvasını ay çekirdeğinden hazırlıyor, kaymakla fırınlayıp bergamotlu ponzu ve kaymak dondurmasıyla servis ediyor. Ziyafet adlı 10 tabaklık tadım menüsü 6.800 lira; tabaklar alakart olarak da seçilebiliyor.
Elbette Ansar’ın tekniği zamanla gelişecek, mutfağı yeni keşiflerle olgunlaşacak. Asıl sevindiğim, kendisinin de bunun farkında olması. Yanlarında kısa süreli çalışmak istediği şefleri şimdiden belirlemiş; yeni mutfaklar tanımaya, başka teknikler öğrenmeye hazırlanıyor.
Hona ’dan ayrılırken aklımda en çok Ansar’ın cesareti, oturttuğu sistem ve kendi kökleriyle kurduğu yaratıcı ilişki kaldı. Bir aile hikâyesini yalnızca menüye yazmakla yetinmemiş, onu lezzete dönüştürmek için emek vermiş. Henüz yolun başında, ama yönünü bulmaya başlamış...

Jack Moylan made his intent clear when speaking to the media in August soon after joining Cardiff City in the summer from Lincoln City.
He outlined how he wanted to impress for the Welsh club and ensure he was a mainstay in Republic of Ireland squads after winning his first two caps in May.
Fast forward three months and the 25-year-old has certainly come good on those promises by stepping up for club and country.
Under fellow Irish man Brian Barry-Murphy at Cardiff he has netted 11 goals in 17 games in all competitions while also providing three assists.
On the international stage, Moylan featured in all four of Republic of Ireland's Nations League games in the extended September/October window, scoring and assisting in a 3-0 win against Israel.
Already a key player for the Bluebirds, Moylan is emerging as an important attacking threat for his country too and will be pivotal in their final two Nations League games against Austria and Kosovo.
It is the latest chapter in the rapid rise of Moylan, who has gone from strength to strength since earning a move to Lincoln in January 2024.
Moylan impressed in Republic of Ireland's 3-0 win over Israel in September, providing a goal and an assist
Moylan joined the Imps from Irish Premier Division side Shelbourne after a stellar final season with the Dublin club in which he finished as the league's joint highest scorer with 15 goals.
At the time of the move, he said it was "the next step" in his career and, after an initial bedding in period and two separate spells on the treatment table with an ankle problem, his and Lincoln's form exploded from November 2025 onwards.
The versatile attacker scored 11 goals and provided six assists last season as Lincoln won promotion and beat Cardiff to the League One title.
His impressive campaign led to a first call-up to the Irish senior squad in May and he marked his debut with a hat-trick in a 5-0 win against Grenada before he was sent off in his second game as they drew with Qatar.
Cardiff came calling in the summer and Moylan made the move to Wales on a four-year deal for an undisclosed fee.
He scored the winner on his debut in the EFL Cup against Swindon and three more followed before the first international break, but he has really kicked on since returning to club duty in early October, proving he has adapted to life in the Championship seamlessly.
Moylan, who has featured as a false nine, a number 10 and off the left this season, has seven goals in his last seven league games, including a first-half hat-trick against West Ham with his first goal a fine finish from outside the box.
His boss at club level told BBC Sport Wales in October that Moylan is a "very exciting player to watch because of how attack-minded he is".
Republic of Ireland fans were treated to snippets of those attacking talents in the first four Nations League games.
After coming off the bench in the defeat against Kosovo, Moylan started the next three games, coming in off the right to link well with Troy Parrott and Adam Idah.
He impressed alongside those two players in the comprehensive win over Israel, setting up Idah's goal before racing through and calmly slotting home.
He was a livewire in the draws that followed against Austria and Israel and is in the frame to continue his burgeoning relationship with star striker Parrott, starting with Saturday's trip to Linz to face Austria.
His international boss Heimir Hallgrimsson knew that he had unearthed a gem from the moment Moylan arrived to train with the senior squad for the first time and hopes there is plenty more to come from him in a green shirt.
"Moylan of course has taken the headlines and taken the spotlight the last couple of weeks and hopefully he can transfer that into the national team," he said.
"His rise has been really fast, but that's brilliant when you find someone in the May [friendly] camp, coming in and scoring three goals in his first game and since then he's been involved in the starting 11 more or less.
"Absolute impact from his first game. Sometimes you need up to 10 games to be comfortable at this level, but he was comfortable from the first minute and from the first training session he had a 'wow' impact."
While it is early days with club and his country, the signs are good that Moylan's trajectory is set to continue on the upward curve it has been trending at over the last two years.

Northern Ireland are top of Nations League Group B2 with eight points from four games
Before this Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland had won just one of 16 games played in the second tier of the competition.
But after eight points from four games across September and October, all without conceding a goal, Michael O'Neill's side could end Saturday night as a League A side for the first time.
For that to come to pass, Hungary would need to lose to Georgia in Tbilisi [17:00 GMT] before a Northern Ireland win at home to Ukraine in the later kick-off.
Even if only they hold up their end of the bargain with a win at Windsor Park, the side would travel to Budapest on Tuesday night knowing a point would be good enough to top the group and seal promotion.
"You do look at the teams that do step up and it's tough. We've seen teams do that before and they find it very difficult," said O'Neill after stressing his side would be looking no further than the first game of this double-header.
"But for us to get that opportunity to play against those big teams in a competitive group stage would be great, it would be great for the development of the team.
"I wouldn't say the results at that point wouldn't be important, but I think we'd learn a lot."

Strong performance in the Nations League carries multiple rewards.
Finishing in the top two of their group - something Northern Ireland would confirm with a draw against Ukraine - would ensure O'Neill's side are among the second group of seeds when the draw for Euro 2028 qualifying is made in Belfast next month.
There is also the potential backdoor route into the qualification play-offs too, the same method used by Northern Ireland to find themselves just two games from the summer's World Cup despite finishing third in their group.
But for O'Neill promotion would also bring the less tangible benefit of showing his squad what is required to reach the very top.
O'Neill has previously sought out friendlies against the likes of Spain and France, drawing praise from his then Les Bleus counterpart Didier Deschamps for taking a game against the latter on the eve of the World Cup when others had not been so keen.
Midfielder Shea Charles previously spoke of how going up against the likes of Spain's Rodri in such fixtures helped "prepare" him for the Premier League before he got his £30m move to Fulham.
And O'Neill feels further exposure to such challenges, especially in regular competitive fixtures, would be hugely beneficial to others in his largely inexperienced side.
He added: "That's good for any player, but particularly young players, because it lets them see what's required, what's required to be a Spanish international and playing in the Champions League or playing your club football at the highest level in Europe.
Birthdays and broken lamps - at home with the Charles brothers
Barnsley midfielder Patrick Kelly scored his first international goal in that game against France, the strike coming on a night he shared the field with the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Michael Olise.
The 22-year-old, who joined the Tykes in the summer of 2025 having not made a senior appearance for West Ham, has played all his club football in either League One, League Two, or the Irish Premiership.
"Playing those bigger nations, it would only improve us as a team," he said.
"You want to test yourself against the best. A couple of the lads have experienced it, they would have played Germany in the last [qualifying ]campaign and done well, and I had it that night against France.
"Playing against the best players in the world, you see where you're at and the team as well."
Having missed that game against France through suspension, Blackburn Rovers defender Tom Atcheson's only international start coming into this campaign had been against Guinea, but the 20-year-old senses the team is ready for the step up.
"I think we do belong there and we're showing it," he said. "We want to have those challenges, we want to challenge ourselves against the best because it's exciting times.
"We know what we're capable of. To get into League A with those massive nations would be unbelievable, that's where we all want to get.
"We're looking forward to the next two games and hopefully to make that happen."

England are three points behind Spain at the top of their Nations League group
Manager Thomas Tuchel will remind England's players of Uefa's anti-racism protocols before Sunday's Nations League fixture against Spain in Madrid.
The match will be England's first in the Spanish capital since a notorious fixture at Real Madrid's Bernabeu stadium in 2004 which was overshadowed by racist chanting aimed at England players.
The Spanish federation was fined last month and ordered to play their next friendly match with a partial stadium closure after fans sang "Islamophobic and xenophobic" chants about Muslims during a game against Egypt.
"We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]," Tuchel said. "There is a protocol in place.
"Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]."
European governing body Uefa, the organiser of the Nations League, has a three-step protocol to handle incidents of discrimination inside stadiums, designed to give referees the power to halt matches, and even abandon games if racist behaviour continues.
In the first instance, referees halt the match and request an announcement on the public address system.
Then, if discrimination continues, officials can stop the game for five to 10 minutes and take the players from the field.
If issues continue after the second stoppage, then the game can be abandoned.
"It's important that the players know about the protocol," Tuchel said.
"And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch."
England's black players such as Ashley Cole and Rio Ferdinand were subject to racist chanting during the 2004 friendly in Madrid
Sunday's fixture takes place at Atletico Madrid's home, the Metropolitano.
Victory would ensure England win their Nations League group and earn a more favourable quarter-final draw but world champions Spain are unbeaten in 43 matches, including a 3-2 win at Wembley in September.
"It's important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength," Tuchel added.
"It [Spain] is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost.
"I think we're there, and I think we're ready to win on Sunday,"

The post-Messi era began with an Argentina defeat on Friday.
Argentina fell to a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in an international friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, marking the team’s first match since Lionel Messi’s international retirement in early October.
Leonardo Balerdi opened the scoring with an own goal in the 48th minute, before Maximiliano Araújo doubled Uruguay’s lead in the 53rd minute under new coach Diego Forlán .
Julián Álvarez pulled one back for the hosts in the 73rd minute.
This clásico rioplatense also kicked off a new chapter for the Argentine national team under Lionel Scaloni, who extended his contract through 2030 earlier this week.
The 39-year-old legend’s retirement remains a fresh wound for Argentine fans; notably, the stadium fell short of a sellout, a rare departure from the norm.
While most supporters in the stands wore the albiceleste jersey with Messi’s iconic No10, Scaloni chose not to assign the number to any player for the match. The coach explained that he has yet to select a successor and, as it is not mandatory, he prefers to leave the jersey vacant for now.
On the pitch, Argentina maintained its signature polished possession, but lacked the explosive, incisive spark that Messi typically delivered in the final third. Neither Nicolás Paz nor Thiago Almada was able to fill that void.
Argentina will look to bounce back against Costa Rica in Córdoba on Tuesday, while Uruguay returns home to host the Dominican Republic on the same day. The Associated Press
